alignments.note: Waw takes the connective And written for it (rule 14).
attah takes now; here the ASV writes the two in the Hebrew's order (rule 14).
hinneh takes behold.
The suffix of hinnenu is realized by the subject pronoun we (rule 40).
Prepositional predicate takes the construction's supplied copula (rule 49).
The construct noun keeps its own word; each morpheme of be-yadekha has an English word of its own, so rule 2 splits the phrase.
Suffix realized by the possessive thy (rule 18).
The preposition takes the as written for it.
Assimilated article token with no the written for it (rules 12, 29).

The substantival adjective is the clause's predicate and takes the construction-supplied it seemeth, which links a predicate adjective rather than predicating an event (rule 20); reading it seemeth as an added lexical verb under rule 20's boundary was the competing analysis.
Waw takes the and written for it (rule 14).
The ASV writes as once and does not repeat it over the second member (rule 22).
Assimilated article token with no the written for it (rules 12, 29).
The second predicate adjective keeps its own word, the copula having joined the first.

CORRECTED: be-ene is a preposition standing before a construct noun for which the ASV writes one English preposition, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is met and the two share a unit headed on the construct noun, as mippene -> before and be-qereb -> among do; the accepted alignment gave unto to the beth alone and left ayin unrepresented, which is the shape rule 30 forbids for a fused expression and rule 22 forbids for a morpheme whose sense the ASV has written inside a word. The chapter fuses be-qirbi, be-qirbo and be-qirbenu to among at 9.7, 9.16 and 9.22 on the same terms. The accepted unit's note disposed only of rule 40's three-way fusion of predicate, preposition and noun, which the written unto does exclude; it does not reach this two-morpheme fusion. Source head is the construct noun under rule 23.
Suffix takes the pronoun thee written for it (rule 18).
The lamed before the infinitive construct takes the written to (rule 52).
Infinitive construct keeps the verb (rule 52).
The preposition takes the unto written for its own relation (rule 11).
Suffix takes the pronoun us (rule 18).
Imperative takes the bare do, no subject pronoun being written for it.

review_notes: Corrected: be-ene is now one fused unit on unto with ayin as source head, replacing the accepted split that gave unto to the beth and left the construct noun unrepresented (rules 22, 30).
be-yadekha in the same verse is split, each of its morphemes holding an English word of its own; only the phrase whose construct noun is left with nothing fuses (rules 2, 30).
it seemeth good is read as the construction's copular frame on the predicate adjective; reading it seemeth as an added lexical verb under rule 20's boundary was the competing analysis.
